item.title: Work Rules Stall as Travel and Tech Shift
item.description: Travel, housing, finance and everyday digital tools changed in several concrete ways.
item.content:encoded:
Travel, housing, finance and everyday digital tools changed in several concrete ways.

  1. Indonesia ferry capsizes with 129 people still missing Indonesia’s Virgo Transport 8 capsized in the Java Sea with 243 people aboard; 108 people were rescued, six deaths were confirmed and 129 people remained missing as rescue operations continued. 14 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  2. Victoria’s two-day work-from-home bill stalls Victoria’s proposed right to work from home two days a week was referred to a parliamentary committee whose report is due 20 October, so the bill will not be voted on before the November state election. 9 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  3. Melbourne home values fall 4.7% over a year Cotality’s August index put Melbourne dwelling values down 1.1% for the month and 4.7% over the year, while Australian dwelling values were 3.6% below their March peak. 1 Sep 2026. Westpac IQ · Follow up
  4. Mathspace breach affects 1.08 million Australian and New Zealand users Mathspace said unauthorised parties accessed an internal reporting system and exposed account information for 1,079,819 users across Australia and New Zealand; passwords, authentication tokens and academic records were not exposed. 7 Sep 2026. ABC · Follow up
  5. Android can now transfer passwords and passkeys directly Android 8+ can now move passwords and passkeys directly between supported password managers without exporting an unencrypted file; Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden and Dashlane already support the transfer flow. 10 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  6. ChatGPT Images 2.5 rolls out to all tiers OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.5 with more precise editing, better reference-photo fidelity, up to 50% lower generation latency, plus Sketch, templates and image comments; it is available across all ChatGPT tiers. 8 Sep 2026. OpenAI · Follow up
  7. ChatGPT Voice can use GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 Astra ChatGPT Voice can now switch to GPT-5.6 or GPT-6 Astra when a conversation requires web search or harder reasoning, expanding the capability available during spoken interactions. 9 Sep 2026. OpenAI · Follow up
  8. Box, Dropbox and SharePoint join ChatGPT Library ChatGPT added Box, Dropbox and SharePoint to Library on the web, letting supported users browse connected files and folders, keep source files beside a conversation and work across selected folders without re-uploading files. 10 Sep 2026. OpenAI · Follow up
  9. Microsoft Entra begins default passkey migration From 1 September, Entra ID users enabled for SMS or voice MFA are automatically enabled for passkeys and nudged to register them; Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication is scheduled to end on 1 February 2027. 1 Sep 2026. Microsoft · Follow up
  10. Gmail, Docs and Keep gain live voice workflows Google launched Gmail Live, Docs Live and Keep Live, using Gemini Audio models for conversational inbox search, spoken document drafting and voice-first note capture, with access depending on the relevant Google AI plan. 3 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  11. Realestate.com.au drops compulsory all-property listing clauses REA Group agreed to remove contract clauses that required agencies to list all properties on realestate.com.au and to change incentives around higher-fee listing products under an ACCC enforceable undertaking. 14 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  12. New Zealand banks lift floating mortgage rates Major New Zealand banks raised floating home-loan rates after the OCR increase; Westpac’s floating and offset rates rose 0.25 percentage points to 6.39% for existing customers from 10 September, while ANZ’s 6.29% floating rate applies to existing loans from 23 September. 10 Sep 2026. Westpac · ANZ · Follow up
  13. Air New Zealand’s Christchurch–Rarotonga route is operating Air New Zealand’s new seasonal nonstop Christchurch–Rarotonga service is operating up to three times weekly through October, creating a direct South Island option to the Cook Islands. 5 Sep 2026. Cook Islands Tourism · Air New Zealand · Follow up
  14. Bee in the City opens on Wellington waterfront Bee in the City is now open with 30 giant bee sculptures around Wellington’s waterfront; the free trail runs from 14 September to 8 November and can be followed with an app or map. 14 Sep 2026. WellingtonNZ · Follow up
  15. GOG adds printable box preservation to classic games GOG expanded its Preservation Program so five classic PC games now include downloadable interactive 3D scans of their original boxes, with printable box files for recreating the physical packaging. 8 Sep 2026. GOG · Follow up
  16. Australian rewards cards face broad September–October repricing Major Australian issuers have announced rewards-card changes around late September and 1 October, including higher purchase rates, lower points earn rates, new caps and reduced insurance on multiple ANZ, NAB, CBA and Westpac products. 10 Sep 2026. Canstar · CommBank · Follow up
  17. AirBaltic files for Chapter 11 while flights continue AirBaltic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New York and secured €350 million in financing; the airline said scheduled operations will continue during the restructuring. 14 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  18. AI-linked shares record sharp falls across Asia AI-linked Asian shares fell sharply on 14 September: SoftBank dropped 13.2%, Kioxia 9.8%, SK Hynix 5.3% and Z.ai 10.5%, while Nasdaq 100 futures were down 1.72% during the broader technology selloff. 14 Sep 2026. Reuters · Reuters markets · Follow up

item.title: Travel Disruptions Spread as Digital Tools Shift
item.description: Travel networks, consumer rules and workplace technology changed in several concrete ways.
item.content:encoded:
Travel networks, consumer rules and workplace technology changed in several concrete ways.

  1. Strait of Hormuz vessel struck and crew evacuated A projectile struck a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on 13 September, causing a fire and forcing the crew to evacuate; UKMTO reported the incident and no group had claimed responsibility when reported. 13 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  2. Revolut confirms sensitive customer-data breach Revolut confirmed that an unauthorised party obtained sensitive customer information after fraudulent requests were sent from a legitimate government-agency email domain; Revolut said its systems and customer funds were not compromised. 12 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  3. Optus outage disrupts emergency calls across four states A 76-minute Optus voice outage on 11 September affected customers in Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the Northern Territory; about 41 Triple Zero calls were referred for welfare checks, with no adverse outcomes reported. 12 Sep 2026. ABC · Follow up
  4. Australia strengthens energy disconnection protections The Australian Energy Market Commission made a final rule requiring energy retailers to contact customers at risk of disconnection through at least two communication channels unless the first contact is acknowledged, while standardising payment-difficulty assistance. 10 Sep 2026. AEMC · Follow up
  5. Australia confirms cash discounts after card-surcharge ban New ACCC guidance confirms businesses may offer clearly disclosed discounts for cash or PayID after major card networks introduce no-surcharge rules on 1 October; the full undiscounted price must remain clearly displayed. 11 Sep 2026. ACCC · BankingDay · Follow up
  6. Australia proposes an opt-out from algorithmic social feeds Draft Digital Duty of Care legislation released for consultation would require social-media platforms to offer Australians a choice between algorithmically recommended content and a feed based on accounts they follow. 8 Sep 2026. Prime Minister of Australia · Reuters · Follow up
  7. Indonesia reopens airports closed by volcanic ash Indonesia reopened all airports that had been closed because of Anak Krakatau ash, including Jakarta’s main airport, reversing the disruption that affected more than 340,000 travellers; some delays could continue while grounded aircraft were inspected. 8 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  8. Italy aviation strikes hit airports and easyJet today Multiple aviation strikes took effect in Italy on 13 September, including a 24-hour easyJet flying-staff action and separate actions affecting security or ground services at Rome, Pisa, Florence, Cagliari, Alghero and Olbia airports. 13 Sep 2026. AeroDue · Follow up
  9. Qatar Airways adds flights to Phuket, Maldives and Vietnam Qatar Airways will increase Doha–Phuket and Doha–Malé services to 21 weekly flights from 25 October and raise Ho Chi Minh City service to 11 weekly flights from 7 November, including four direct weekly flights. 10 Sep 2026. Qatar Airways · Follow up
  10. UK air-traffic failure cancels more than 2,000 flights A UK air-traffic-control flight-processing failure on 8 September led to more than 2,000 flight cancellations across at least 15 airports; the technical fault was fixed the same day but disruption continued into 9 September. 9 Sep 2026. AP · Follow up
  11. Auckland City Rail Link starts carrying passengers Auckland’s City Rail Link opened to passenger services on 13 September, with trains running through the new city-centre stations for the first time and a new network timetable taking effect. 13 Sep 2026. Auckland Transport · Follow up
  12. SH2 Melling overnight lane restrictions begin From the evening of 13 September, southbound State Highway 2 between Melling Link and the Normandale Road overbridge is reduced to one lane from 7pm to 5am on five nights, with two further five-night work blocks later in September. 13 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  13. Gemini launches a native Windows desktop app Google released the Gemini desktop app for Windows 10 and 11, available now to personal users and Google Workspace customers, with an Alt+Space overlay plus access to Workspace information and image generation. 11 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  14. ChatGPT Work launches a Data agent OpenAI launched a Data agent in ChatGPT Work that can connect to approved company data sources, investigate metric changes, build interactive dashboards and work with BI tools including Power BI, Tableau and Oracle BI. 10 Sep 2026. OpenAI · Follow up
  15. Power BI Q&A retirement moves to February 2027 Microsoft extended Power BI Q&A’s retirement from December 2026 to February 2027; after retirement the Q&A visual will be removed and existing reports containing it will show an error in its place. 11 Sep 2026. Magnetism · Follow up
  16. Gemini gains cross-app task orchestration Google began rolling out Gemini actions that can create content, schedule events and coordinate tasks across Workspace apps while respecting user permissions and requiring review for external communication or calendar commitments. 9 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  17. Australia changes foreign-investment fee payment methods From 19 September, Australia’s Treasury will stop accepting credit and debit cards for foreign-investment fees; BPAY, direct deposit and international bank transfer remain available. 11 Sep 2026. Australian Treasury · Follow up
  18. Kuranda Scenic Railway closes for bridge repairs Queensland Rail closed the Kuranda Range to rail traffic through 20 September after finding a bridge defect, cancelling Kuranda Scenic Railway services and arranging a free road-coach loop for eligible pre-booked passengers. 10 Sep 2026. Queensland Rail · Follow up
